ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a DC power supply labeled Vsource = 30 V. The upper end of the power supply passes through a series resistor labeled Rseries, with a value of 2.2 kΩ, to reach the output node. From this node downward, a Zener diode labeled Vz = 12.5 V is connected in parallel to ground, and on the right side there is also a load resistor Rload connected from the same node to ground. The problem gives Rload = 4 kΩ. Reasoning calculation: According to the method, assume the Zener diode is in the voltage-regulating state, so the output node voltage is Vz = 12.5 V. The series resistor current is Is = (30 - 12.5) / 2.2 kΩ = 17.5 / 2200 A = 7.9545 mA. The load current is IL = 12.5 / 4 kΩ = 12.5 / 4000 A = 3.125 mA. The Zener current equals the series current minus the load current: Izener = Is - IL = 7.9545 - 3.125 = 4.8295 mA, approximately 4.83 mA.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram and extract Vs = 30 V, Rs = 2.2 kΩ, Vz = 12.5 V, and Rload = 4 kΩ.
